links.targetTitle: The Atlas manufactures case law in advance through hypotheti
The Core Facilitator holds broad discretion to resolve Atlas

title: The Atlas separates adjudication doctrine from adjudication history using two distinct document types
content:
Two Supporting Document types sit side by side and are easy to conflate. **Facilitator Action Tenets** (A.1.2.2.2.12, at .0.4.X) contain "the adjudication logic, principle or doctrine that is directly derived from the Target Document." **Facilitator Action Precedents** (A.1.2.2.2.14, at .0.5.X) "record all the relevant data related to a Facilitator Action, to serve as precedent for future Facilitator Actions."

The distinction is prospective versus retrospective. A Tenet is written *before* any dispute, distilling what the rule implies for adjudication; A.1.2.2.2.11 makes consultation mandatory — "when a controversy concerns the Target Document, the Facilitators must consult and apply the pertinent Action Tenet(s) in their decision-making." A Precedent is written *after* an action, as an input/output/label record of what happened.

Tenets also carry an explicit extrapolation aid: they may include "policy statements" highlighting the values served by adhering to the Tenet, because "when facing edge cases, these policy statements can help Facilitators to extrapolate from the Tenet's logic." This is purpose-encoding one level down from the Spirit — each rule gets its own local statement of why, so extrapolation does not have to reach all the way back to the Preamble.

A.1.2.2.2.12 also states where Tenets are needed: mostly for Immutable Document types, "as these tend to have generalized, broad language," and often not for Core Documents whose language is "far more specific and concrete." Abstraction, not importance, drives the need for doctrine — but the Atlas refuses to hard-code it: "the determination... should always be tailor-made."
description: Facilitator Action Tenets (.0.4.X) state principles derived from a rule and must be consulted in any controversy about it; Facilitator Action Precedents (.0.5.X) record what was actually decided.
